MOZ.note: Only a drafted procurement ToR and a refocus of procurement on mobile ID and PKI; nothing contracted, piloted or in service.

facts.fact: The World Bank ISR says a QR code added to birth certificates enhances data exchange with the ID registry, and a new campaign process is integrated with DNIC processes, while the project target is interoperability of birth and health information systems.
facts.system: QR code on birth certificate / DNIC integrated process

facts.fact: The World Bank ISR reports 4,574,257 individuals registered in the civil registration database (e-SIRCEV) at 20 March 2026 against a 13,000,000 target, with a backlog-scanning pilot held in Maputo and Matola.

The World Bank ISR says the government interoperability platform is available in a test environment with a data exchange proof of concept completed, X-Road linkage software developed and a contract signed, against a target of 15 interoperable public systems by December 2026.

MOZ.note: Document states nothing on a national digital strategy.

facts.fact: The World Bank ISR says the citizen service portal offers 25 information services and a first transactional municipal land property service was added in the pilot of its earlier version, which was discontinued; a new portal contract is signed with operation expected by June 2026 against a target of 15 transactional and 40 information services.

MOZ.note: No unique ID number issued at birth is stated; birth and ID integration is only a QR code and campaign process.

facts.fact: The World Bank ISR says an identity verification API from DNIC awaits feedback from institutions, with zero relying parties using the verification services at 20 March 2026 against a target of six.

MOZ.note: Only a municipal land property request service on the citizen portal, being added and from a discontinued portal version; no land register stated.
Only a backlog scanning pilot (archive) and a central e-SIRCEV record count; no statement of how local offices make the record.
